blurb: A place to run commands. One call can start it and mount a Branch.
reasons: Why --mount on create: an agent's first calls are create, mount, exec. One call that answers the handle exec takes saves a round trip, and the mount is workspace mount itself, so it adds no second way to mount.
Why remove, not close: the call deletes the Sandbox, its runtime and its record. Every other thing is removed with remove.

Why list rows carry Workspace handles: the handle is what every Workspace call takes. Where the home records it, the list gives it for nothing; where a machine's worker keeps it, the row says so and workspace list asks.
Why sandbox list asks no machine: a state comes from records and costs no probe. sandbox get is the call that asks one Sandbox.

calls.note: with --mount B the call also mounts Branch B and answers the Workspace handle and its path, as workspace mount does, under the same default name (the Branch's name made valid); the call has no name option of its own, so a name already in use is the mount's Exists refusal, whose fix names workspace mount … --name; without it {"ok":true}. If the Sandbox starts and the mount is refused, the Sandbox is kept (ready): the call is refused with the mount's own code, and the refusal carries sandbox and a fix naming layerfs workspace mount. --machine defaults to the machine of the project's sqlite Store; a project of a PostgreSQL Store runs on this computer (native) without it, as today: the Store itself records no machine. The names native, docker and *.root stay refused. With --image the image is copied as machine load-image copies it, and the call refuses what that call refuses, with the same shapes (Capacity included); the copy's lock is held until the Sandbox is built on the image, so a machine prune --unused meanwhile leaves it. Progress phases: inspect, lock, export, send (bytes), unpack, start, then mount with --mount

calls.new_work: `--mount` is new: today create and mount are two calls. One call must start the Sandbox, record it, then run the mount; a refused mount must leave the Sandbox recorded and ready and answer a refusal that carries `sandbox` and a `fix` (`layerfs workspace mount <sandbox> <branch>`). The mount's default name (the Branch's name made valid) is new work of `workspace.mount`; this call takes no name option. `ok` is true in every long answer; `workspace` and `path` are null there without `--mount`. The default machine is today's: the sqlite Store's machine, else `native`. The record's `runtime` (the same word as `backend`) and `id` leave the answer; `created` (milliseconds) becomes `created_at`. v19: the image copy's lock is held until the Sandbox is built on the image (today it is let go when the copy ends, and a `machine prune --unused` in between removes the image just copied); the `lock` phase and the load-image refusal shapes are as `machine load-image`'s.

calls.note: records only: the call asks no machine. A row leaves state out when ready; the state is the last one a record holds, so lost or not_answering shows here only after a sandbox get saw it. workspaces are its mounted Workspaces, each {workspace, branch}, listed only where the home keeps the Workspace records (a Sandbox on native, or one reached directly) and the Sandbox is not blocked. Elsewhere the machine's worker keeps them: the row says workspaces_not_listed:true while that machine is ready, and workspace list --sandbox S asks it. A Sandbox on a stopped machine answers blocked with blocked_by naming the machine, and no Workspaces (long form: workspaces is null). [project] → --project; --live is gone: sandbox get asks one Sandbox, and machine stats counts a machine's running daemons

calls.new_work: `state` and its companions are new on a row: today a row carries the record's own word (`creating`, `closing`, `unresolved`, `gone`, `running`). From records: a recorded `op` is `busy` (`op.name` is `create` or `remove`), an operation whose outcome is not known is `broken` with `reason: unresolved`, a record with no runtime id is `broken` with `reason: missing`, a record of the retired docker backend is `broken` with `reason: unsupported`, and a machine that is not ready makes it `blocked`; `broken` with `reason: lost` or `not_answering` appears once a `sandbox get` saw it and wrote it to the record; every `fix` is `layerfs sandbox remove <sandbox>`, and the long form's `message` is the sentence behind a `blocked` or `broken` state. `workspaces` and `workspaces_not_listed` are new: each handle and Branch come from the Workspace records the home keeps, which needs every Workspace to have a name (new work of `workspace.mount`). `--machine` is new. `--cursor` is new: today the call pages by position (`page_size`, `page_pos`, default 50).

calls.note: asks the Sandbox's own side, as today: its daemon lists the Workspaces. No paging: a Sandbox holds at most 16 Workspaces (workspace_capacity). Each Workspace answers its handle, its Branch and the exec ids of the commands running in it; a Workspace leaves state out when ready (busy while it mounts, commits or unmounts; broken after a failure). On a machine that is not ready the Sandbox answers blocked and no Workspaces (long form: workspaces is null); when its machine does not answer the Sandbox is unknown with observed_at (when its state was last known) and no Workspaces, never blocked; a Sandbox whose machine says it does not run is broken with reason: lost, and one whose daemon admits no connection is broken with reason: not_answering. --with stats adds the daemon's process, the Sandbox's CPU and memory and each Workspace's overlay size

calls.new_work: The state table is new: today the call answers the record's word (`creating`, `closing`, `unresolved`, `gone`, `lost`, `running`) with `down_reason` and `down`. The mapping: a live `op` is `busy` (`op.name` `create` or `remove`; today's op carries `started` in milliseconds and `uncertain`); an uncertain op is `broken`/`unresolved`; no runtime id, or a confirmed stop, is `broken`/`missing`; the retired docker backend is `broken`/`unsupported`; a machine that is stopped, busy or broken makes it `blocked`; a machine that does not answer makes it `unknown` with `observed_at` and `workspaces` null (the call is a live read; today it is refused or answers `down_reason`); a machine that says the Sandbox does not run is `broken`/`lost`; a daemon that admits no connection is `broken`/`not_answering` (today's `down {code, resource, pool_vacant, reserved_vacant, retained}` becomes the long form's `message`, the sentence behind a `blocked` or `broken` state). Every `fix` is `layerfs sandbox remove <sandbox>`. As a live read the call writes the Sandbox's record only when the state word or its reason changes (that write moves `generation`), so `sandbox list` and the tree then show `lost` or `not_answering` from records; `observed_at` is kept beside the record in an observation file that `generation` does not cover. A Workspace's `state` is new, from the daemon's `activity`: `idle` is `ready`; `attaching`, `committing` and `closing` are `busy` with `op.name` `mount`, `commit` and `unmount` (the daemon records no start time for them today); `uncertain` is `broken`/`unresolved` and `local_failure` is `broken`/`failed`, each with `fix: layerfs workspace unmount <workspace> --discard --force`. `mounted_at` is the Workspace record's `created`; where the worker keeps that record the reply must carry it. `--with stats` regroups what the call always answers today (`daemon`, `usage`, `usage_reason`, `daemon_capacity`, and each Workspace's `overlay_bytes` and `usage`), with `cpu_usec` as `cpu_ms`, `memory_current` as `memory_bytes`, `pids` as `pid_count` and `oom_kills` as `oom_kill_count`. Renames per Workspace: `ws` to `workspace`, the 64-hex `workspace` to `id`, `base` to `commit`, `head_moved_since_mount` to `branch_moved`, `running[].exec_id` to `commands[].exec` with `started` as `started_at`. `namespace`, `root`, `revision`, `directory`, `mounted`, `dirty`, `activity`, `name` and `next_page_pos` leave the answer (`workspace status` answers the overlay counts).

calls.note: renamed from close: it stops the Sandbox and deletes its runtime and its record. Without --force it is refused Busy while a command runs (the refusal lists the exec ids as running) and InUse while a Workspace is mounted (it lists workspaces). With --force each running command is cancelled first; one whose cancel is not confirmed refuses the call Unknown and nothing more is done. unmounted lists the Workspaces a forced removal ended: their uncommitted changes are gone. A Sandbox of the retired docker backend is forgotten: its container is left, with the fix line that removes it. left says what may remain on its machine unrecorded. A lost reply leaves the record broken with reason: unresolved; another sandbox remove settles it
calls.help: stop a Sandbox and remove it

options.name: force
options.help: remove it even while Workspaces are mounted or commands run; uncommitted changes are lost

calls.new_work: The rename (no alias, R1). `outcome` is `removed`, `already_gone` (its runtime was gone; today `was_gone` and the unstarted case) or `forgotten` (the retired docker backend). `unmounted` holds Workspace handles: today's `unknown` lists their paths. Today's `remove: "docker rm -f ..."` is `fix`. `left` is a list of sentences in every case (today a text on one outcome and a list on another). The refusal while a Workspace is mounted is `InUse` (`MountsActive` today) and lists `workspaces`; the `Busy` refusal lists `running` (`detail.execs` today). Progress is new: today the call records its op (phase `stop`) and takes no `on_progress`; the events are the op's phases, `cancel` (forced, one per command), `stop` and `delete`.

calls.note: UI only; the same shape as machine files. Without path: the Sandbox's roots, each with a role (workspace with its handle, home, log, and root where it has one). A folder answers items, one page in tree order to --depth levels; a file answers one byte window: text, with next_byte_offset while more follows, or binary:true with its size when it is not text. type is file, dir or symlink, and other for a device, socket or pipe; not_read says why an entry is listed and not read (mount, restricted, system, unreadable). Limits as today: depth 32, 1000 entries, a 1 MiB window. Writes no call-log line. On a machine that is not ready the call is refused Unavailable

calls.new_work: Renames only, on the code that exists: `entries` to `items`, `next`/`has_more` to `next_cursor`, `kind` to `type` (`folder` is `dir`; `mount`, `restricted`, `system` and `unreadable` are a `dir` with `not_read`), `content` to `text` and a file's `next` to `next_byte_offset`, `mtime` (milliseconds) to `modified_at`, `mode` to octal text. A root's `workspace` is the handle (the 64-hex id today). The default page is 100 entries (500 today). A page the walk ends early (`reason: limit` or `deadline` today) ends with a `next_cursor`.

calls.note: was logs.sandbox: the Sandbox's daemon log, the same shape as machine log. The first call answers the last --limit lines, oldest first; next_cursor continues with the lines before them and is left out at the start of the log. A call reads at most 64 KiB, so it may answer fewer lines; a line longer than that comes in pieces, each but the last with continued:true. A line is raw text: the daemon writes no time or level. Reading the lines after a cursor (to follow a log) is gone: a log pages backwards only, and a client that follows one reads the newest page again. On a machine that is not ready the call is refused Unavailable. Writes no call-log line, as today

calls.note: checks the Sandbox (its record, its runtime, its daemon), then each of its Workspaces from the daemon's list (workspace.mounted, workspace.activity); a Workspace has no doctor of its own. Short: {"ok":true}, or findings and not_checked. A not_checked entry carries blocked_by (its machine is not ready: no live check is tried) or reason (timeout, busy, lost). No --timeout: each thing has its own time budget. --progress sends one event per finished thing, the Sandbox (self) then each Workspace (workspaces). The call repairs nothing and exits 0 once its report is made

calls.new_work: The table call and the one doctor shape are new: today `layerfs doctor sandbox <sandbox>` is a shell command outside the call table, with its own report (`checks` with outcomes pass, fail, unknown, skipped and blocked). The Sandbox's checks exist and keep their ids (`checks.sandbox`, in the order they run); the ids that go are in `off_table`; `unknown` and `skipped` become `not_checked` with a `reason`, `blocked` becomes `not_checked` with `blocked_by`. Per-Workspace nodes are new: today one check, `sandbox.workspaces`, covers the daemon's whole list (`sandbox.doctor_workspaces` rows carry `mounted` and `activity`); it becomes `workspace.mounted` and `workspace.activity` on one node per Workspace, which needs each row's handle. Progress events are new. A per-thing time budget replaces the call's one budget.
